title: C1029 — EVAP purge valve connector
introduction:
The evaporative emission (EVAP) purge valve meters stored fuel vapor toward the engine intake. I use this reference as its electrical address book: the identity table describes the connector, the drawing locates the labeled cavities, and the assignment table connects those labels to circuit functions. The valve manages vapor flow; this page maps its electrical connections.

Read each assignment row across from Cavity to Terminal Part Number. Repeated cavity entries have different gauge and terminal details; they do not identify extra positions in the drawing. The functions distinguish the powertrain controller’s purge-valve circuit from the fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply. The pigtail table then provides a separate service-parts cross-reference.

This is an identification guide, not a probing, wire-selection or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are not established here. The summary’s pin-count entry also conflicts with the drawing and pigtail cavity count; that disagreement remains unresolved.

edits.why: I use the cavity labels and surrounding housing outline together to navigate the drawing. As displayed, the upper cavity maps to the supply and the lower cavity to purge-valve control. The projection on the right is a housing feature; the illustration does not establish its release function or the physical viewing direction.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: The Cavity column links each row to the drawing; Circuit Number identifies the circuit, while Function explains its role. Read the gauge and terminal fields together within each row. The repeated control-circuit entry is not permission to choose either terminal interchangeably, and the supply description retains the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative.

A pigtail is a connector with attached wire leads. I distinguish its Service Part from the Engineering Shell identifier and keep its gauge and material details separate from the circuit-assignment rows. This is a parts cross-reference; it does not teach splicing or establish a replacement decision.

originalAuthorHold: The identity table states Pin Count 3, but the connector drawing labels only cavities 1 and 2 and the pigtail table states Cavities 2. Preserve all original data and resolve this conflict before treating the summary pin count as authoritative.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all31 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and3 edits. PinCount3 versus pictured1–2/kit2 and repeated CE113 gauge/terminal applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
